Include vehicle keys in Android backup
Key backup needs Android 12 or newer.
Currently: vehicle keys are stored so Android can back them up. Google backups are encrypted with your Google account and device lock, so a new phone can restore pairing from them.
Currently: vehicle keys are stored without Keystore encryption, and Android 11 and below leave them out of backups.
Currently: vehicle keys are encrypted with this device\'s hardware-backed Keystore (AES). An Android backup can\'t restore them on another phone, so a new phone needs re-pairing with an NFC card tap.

Android decides when to back up (usually daily, while idle and charging). Check or trigger one in system Settings \u2192 Backup. Android restores it during phone setup, a device transfer, or an app install when automatic restore is on; otherwise restore it manually or re-pair.
Your home electricity price. It shows what a charge session cost beside the car\'s charge details; leave it empty to hide that. A new price applies from the start of the latest charge.
Export failed. A partial file may remain; delete it.

Saves the raw history, what the car sent and what the app did, as a zip you choose the place for, for example to attach to a bug report. It holds locations and drive details. It stays on the phone until you share it.
Each car has its own key, and pairing always enrolls a freshly generated one. Stored keys are kept, and a car that still has its key is marked paired by the next whitelist check.
Include vehicle keys in Android backup?

This applies to every car you have paired. Currently each vehicle key is encrypted with this device\'s hardware-backed Keystore (AES), so only this phone can use it. Turning this on stores the keys so Android backup can restore them on a new phone; Google backups are encrypted with your Google account and device lock, so exposure requires someone who can restore your backup and unlock your phone. Near the car, that person could read vehicle data and control charging — they cannot unlock or drive, and new keys still need the NFC card tap plus vehicle confirmation. If you turn this off later, older backup copies may remain until they are replaced.
New backups can\'t restore the keys on another phone, but usable copies already in Android backup may remain until they are replaced.
The app forgets each car\'s cached Bluetooth address and pairing slots, so the next scan finds the cars again at their current addresses. The cars, their stored keys and their history stay.
Car cache cleared. Scan to find and reconnect your cars.
Lets the app find your Tesla over Bluetooth and open the encrypted link to read its battery state. This is Android\'s \"Nearby devices\" permission.
Android only lets apps scan iBeacon-style Bluetooth devices with location permission. Allow it once here: the app never reads your location, and nothing leaves the phone.
If you use Do Not Disturb while driving, add this app to its exceptions so trip notifications still pop up.
Android shows a notification while the app tracks your car in the background. This one is optional, but without it tracking runs silently.
Android will not show the permission dialog again. Open app settings to allow it.
Permission denied. You can try again.
TeslaBatteryBLE talks to your Tesla directly over Bluetooth. A few permissions are needed first; each one is explained as we go.
Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Tesla, Inc.
A local-first Tesla BLE battery tracker. It reads battery data over Bluetooth and keeps the history on the phone: no account, no cloud, nothing leaves the phone.
TeslaBatteryBLE is free software, built in spare time. If it is useful to you, you can support development through GitHub Sponsors.
TeslaBatteryBLE is AGPL-3.0-only. Bundled libraries (Wire, AndroidX, Kotlin) are Apache-2.0.
No browser app found to open this link.
Rated range in miles when the car was new; it sets the baseline for state of health.
Enter the VIN first: it gives the model and year.
Parked and awake: the app reads the car every %1$s so it can sleep. Next read at %2$s. Refresh to read now.
Doesn\'t match this car\'s advertised name
Add your VIN to read and control this car

This car\'s Bluetooth session uses its VIN, so the app cannot read or control it without one. The easiest way to get it is to copy it from the Tesla app. It is checked against the car\'s advertised name, stays on the phone and is never logged.
Saved for this car; never logged.
Tesla app not installed. The VIN is also printed on the windshield or the driver\'s door jamb.
The easiest way is to copy it from the Tesla app.
TeslaBatteryBLE needs Bluetooth access to find and talk to your car. Nothing leaves the phone.
Turn it on to find your car. The app reconnects by itself.
Location permission denied; using the system chooser fallback
Location services are off. BLE scans return no results until it is enabled.
Keep the app open and stay near the car.
Car is asleep. Waking it to open the charge port\u2026
Full range times the car\'s rated constant. That lands on the full-pack energy a CAN tool reports, buffer included, although the range itself stops above the buffer. Usable energy is about 3kWh less.
Below 0%% the car holds estimated of up to %1$s buffer range.
Rated range from 100% down to 0%. The car still holds about 3kWh (the buffer) below 0%, so this range does not include it.
Full range divided by the new-car rated range. To match the degradation your CAN tool shows, adjust the rated range in Edit car (the pencil).
Worst and best case at that point: the drain could be two standard errors faster or slower than measured, from how much the parked readings scatter around the line.
Power-down drain: the rate over the stretches the car sat parked with nobody in it and Sentry and climate off, an hour or more apart, the quietest the battery drains. The dashed line follows it.
Parked drain over all parked time, powered down or not. Once enough power-down time is measured, this switches to the power-down rate.

On: Android waits for the car and connects when it comes into range. Off: the app connects straight to the last address and scans when that fails. Takes effect on the next connection. Debug builds only.
Adds the simulated car to the next scan, alongside the real ones. Debug builds only.
Pops up when a trip or navigation starts, then updates quietly.
Your energy price times the energy the drive used, per 100 distance units.
Fewer stats and coarser steps until the car\'s full range is learned.
Asleep the whole time - only when watched by the phone at least every 10min.
The rate over the %1$s between the nearest readings. The sleep may have been interrupted for up to %2$s of that.
The slowest battery loss between two readings at least 6 hours apart while parked.
The odometer unchanged and not charging.
Parked, unoccupied, Sentry and climate off. The car may still be awake when disconnected but expected to go sleep.
